--- title: "[QuantileGAM]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Non-crossing quantile GAM. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/quantile_gam.py#L104-L520){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python QuantileGAM(formula, quantiles=None, *, sigma=0.1, non_crossing=True) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Fits a separate additive quantile regression model for each requested quantile level `tau`, and enforces the natural ordering constraint that quantile curves must not cross: for `tau_1 < tau_2`, the fitted curve `q_{tau_1}(x)` must lie at or below `q_{tau_2}(x)` at every observed covariate combination. Ordinary quantile GAMs, fit independently for each `tau`, provide no such guarantee and can produce curves that cross, especially in regions with sparse data or heavy smoothing. Use `QuantileGAM` whenever you need multiple quantiles of a conditional distribution (e.g. to build a prediction interval or characterize skewness/heteroscedasticity) and want the estimated quantiles to respect the required monotone ordering in `tau`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [formula]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Formula]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Model formula (e.g. `"y ~ s(x)"`), shared across all quantile levels; only the loss function differs between them. [quantiles]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[float] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Quantile levels to fit. Must be in `(0, 1)` and will be sorted. Defaults to `[0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9]`. [sigma]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Bandwidth of the smoothed pinball ("extended log-F", ELF) loss used to approximate the non-differentiable quantile check loss. Smaller `sigma` more closely approximates the true quantile loss but can slow IRLS convergence; use `calibrate_sigma()` to select it via cross-validation. [non_crossing]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), enforce the non-crossing constraint via iterative isotonic projection. If `False`, quantiles are fit completely independently and may cross. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} Each quantile is fit by minimizing a smoothed pinball loss (the ELF loss of Fasiolo et al. 2021), which approximates the quantile check function $$\rho_\tau(u) = u \, (\tau - \mathbb{1}[u < 0])$$ with a twice-differentiable surrogate suitable for IRLS. After each round of fitting, the vector of fitted quantiles at every observation, `[q_{\tau_1}(x_i), \dots, q_{\tau_k}(x_i)]`, is checked for monotonicity; if it is violated anywhere, the vector is projected onto the monotone non-decreasing cone via the pool-adjacent-violators algorithm (PAVA), following the "stepwise projection" strategy of Bondell, Reich, & Wang (2010). The projected fitted values are then used to re-derive coefficients (via a least-squares refit against the corrected working response), and the cycle repeats for up to `max_iter` rounds or until no crossings remain. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#78ce646a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np from whittaker.quantile_gam import QuantileGAM rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 500 x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n) y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + rng.normal(scale=0.2 + 0.3 * x, size=n) model = QuantileGAM("y ~ s(x)", quantiles=[0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9]) model.fit({"x": x, "y": y}) preds = model.predict({"x": x[:5]}) # dict of tau -> PredictionResult print(model.crossing_fraction()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 0.0 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
formula The parsed model formula shared by every quantile level.
is_fitted Whether `fit()` has been called successfully.
non_crossing Whether the non-crossing constraint is enforced.
quantiles Quantile levels fitted by this model, in ascending order.
sigma Bandwidth of the smoothed pinball (ELF) loss used for every quantile.
### [formula]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} The parsed model formula shared by every quantile level. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [formula]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Formula]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ### [is_fitted]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Whether `fit()` has been called successfully. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [is_fitted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ### [non_crossing]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Whether the non-crossing constraint is enforced. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [non_crossing]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ### [quantiles]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Quantile levels fitted by this model, in ascending order. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [quantiles]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ### [sigma]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Bandwidth of the smoothed pinball (ELF) loss used for every quantile. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [sigma]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
coverage() Compute empirical coverage of the outermost quantile interval.
crossing_fraction() Fraction of observations where quantile curves cross.
fit() Fit the quantile GAM.
predict() Predict quantiles on new data.
predict_interval() Return prediction interval from the lowest and highest quantiles.
summary() Return a text summary of the fitted quantile GAM.
### [coverage()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute empirical coverage of the outermost quantile interval. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/quantile_gam.py#L436-L456){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python coverage(data=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [InputData | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Data to evaluate on. Defaults to the training data. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fraction of observations within `[q_low, q_high]`. ::: ### [crossing_fraction()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fraction of observations where quantile curves cross. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/quantile_gam.py#L458-L484){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python crossing_fraction(data=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [InputData | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Data to evaluate on. Defaults to the training data. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fraction of observations with at least one crossing (0.0 if non-crossing constraint is satisfied everywhere). ::: ### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the quantile GAM. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/quantile_gam.py#L257-L349){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit(data, *, method="REML", max_iter=5, select=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Fits a separate ELF-based `GAM` for every quantile level in `self.quantiles`. When `non_crossing=True`, this is repeated for up to `max_iter` rounds: after each round, the fitted quantile curves are checked for crossing violations and, if found, corrected via isotonic projection (see class Notes); the corrected values are used to re-derive each quantile model's coefficients before the next round of refitting. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [InputData]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Column-oriented data containing the response and all covariates in `formula`. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["REML"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Smoothing parameter selection method applied to every quantile's `GAM` fit: `"GCV"`, `"REML"` (default), or `"ML"`. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[5]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of non-crossing projection iterations. Each iteration fits all quantiles and projects to enforce ordering. Ignored when `non_crossing=False` (in which case a single independent fit per quantile is performed). [select]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, enable double-penalty variable selection for each quantile's `GAM`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [QuantileGAM]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns `self` for method chaining. ::: ### [predict()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict quantiles on new data. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/quantile_gam.py#L351-L397){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict(new_data, *, se=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Predicts each quantile level's `GAM` independently on `new_data`, then, if `non_crossing=True`, re-applies the isotonic projection across quantile levels at each new observation so the returned predictions never cross, even if the fitted models happen to disagree slightly on out-of-sample covariate combinations. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [new_data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [InputData]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : New covariate data. [se]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, include standard errors for each quantile's linear predictor. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[float, PredictionResult]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dict mapping quantile level to predictions. ::: ### [predict_interval()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return prediction interval from the lowest and highest quantiles. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/quantile_gam.py#L399-L434){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict_interval(new_data, lower_tau=None, upper_tau=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [new_data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [InputData]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : New covariate data. [lower_tau]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Lower quantile level. Defaults to the smallest fitted quantile. [upper_tau]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Upper quantile level. Defaults to the largest fitted quantile. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[NDArray, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(lower, upper)` prediction bounds. ::: ### [summary()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return a text summary of the fitted quantile GAM. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/quantile_gam.py#L486-L511){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python summary() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Reports the formula, fitted quantile levels, non-crossing setting, and ELF `sigma`, followed by one line per quantile giving its `GAM`'s total effective degrees of freedom and deviance. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Multi-line, human-readable summary suitable for printing. :::
